`__all__ = [name for name in globals() if name.startswith('test_')]` is safe on CPython 3.10-3.14. globals() returns the module namespace even inside a comprehension that is not inlined (3.10/3.11), unlike dir()/locals(). It exports the 8 test functions (12 cases with parametrization) and not the helper native_module. The parametrize marks stay on the function objects and monkeypatch still resolves when the functions are re-exported. Grep found no other definitions of these 8 names under tests/, and the import guard in curated_contracts.py at line 43 would raise ImportError on any shadowing.

The apply gates are adequate. It requires an APPROVE decision whose hashes equal the plan and script, matches the registry hash, checks the owner marker and the exact root set, and runs clean_target (no .git ancestor of the clone root; no overlap with protected or blocked paths). It then re-checks every file and directory for exact membership, identity, mtime, size, sha, nlink==1 and no_alias (which refuses reparse points), plus the bundle hashes. Only after that does Remove-Item -LiteralPath run, behind a canonical-path guard. Remaining risks: (a) there is a small time-of-check/time-of-use window before Remove-Item; (b) the bundles are checked by hash only and not re-verified with git; (c) Windows PowerShell 5.1's Remove-Item -Recurse has a history of trouble with junctions. The per-entry reparse check just before deletion mitigates (c), and all of these are acceptable for owned, current-run scratch. The script writes its log with mode 'xb' and records the actual exit and wait. The pytest case parent directories stay in place for the ordinary managed cleanup.
